title: How do I connect?
intro: The phone and this computer must be on the same network. They do not need the internet, and no mobile data is used: the records only travel between the two devices.

ways.title: Same router (cable or Wi-Fi)
ways.needs: Nothing extra. This is the most common way.
steps: Connect this computer to your router with a network cable, or join the router's Wi-Fi.
Connect the phone to the same router's Wi-Fi. Avoid guest or public Wi-Fi: many of them stop devices from seeing each other.
On the phone, open Connect to desktop and scan the code shown here.
ways.worked: The phone shows this computer's name and asks you to wait while it is approved here.

ways.title: Phone hotspot
ways.needs: This computer needs Wi-Fi, or a small USB Wi-Fi stick.
steps: On the phone, switch on the hotspot (tethering).
On this computer, join the phone's hotspot like any Wi-Fi.
Close and open this window again, so the code shows the new address.
On the phone, open Connect to desktop and scan the code.
ways.worked: The line at the top of this window says this computer is on a network.

ways.title: USB cable (tethering)
ways.needs: Only a USB cable and a USB port. No Wi-Fi and no router.
steps: Plug the phone into this computer with a USB cable.
On the phone, open Settings and switch on USB tethering. Windows then sets up a small network over the cable.
Close and open this window again, so the code shows the new address.
On the phone, open Connect to desktop and scan the code.
ways.worked: The line at the top of this window says this computer is on a network.

ways.title: Hotspot from this computer
ways.needs: This computer needs a Wi-Fi adapter.
steps: On this computer, open Windows Settings, then Network and internet, then Mobile hotspot, and switch it on.
On the phone, join the hotspot using the name and password Windows shows.
Close and open this window again, so the code shows the new address.
On the phone, open Connect to desktop and scan the code.
ways.worked: The line at the top of this window says this computer is on a network.

ifStuck: If Windows asks whether to allow FleetPilot through its firewall, choose Allow on private networks.
If the phone cannot see this computer, check that both show the same Wi-Fi name, and that this window is still open.
If the camera is not allowed, type the address and the PIN shown here into the phone instead.
If nothing works, use the USB cable way: it needs no Wi-Fi at all.
noNetwork: No network was found on this computer. The easiest fix is the USB cable way below: it needs no Wi-Fi and no router.
